siteSettings.heroThesis: I turn customer problems into products and workflows that work. I'm a product manager with an operations foundation, leading discovery, product strategy, and delivery across B2B SaaS, commerce, and enterprise platforms. I also design and build prototypes to test ideas early and give teams a clearer direction.
siteSettings.problemLead: Where are users getting stuck, and what is it costing the business?
siteSettings.problemBody: I start with customer discovery and the operational reality behind the request: where people lose time, where users drop off, and where teams keep solving the same problem manually.
siteSettings.betLead: Test the idea before committing the team.
siteSettings.betBody: I use research, experiments, and prototypes to decide what deserves investment. At QShop, that meant testing the activation flow. At Sugar Guest Pro, it meant validating workflows through WhatsApp. At QTrack, it meant deciding when to stop.
siteSettings.outcomeLead: Better activation. Less manual work. Clearer delivery.
siteSettings.aboutHero: Start with the user's problem. Build the business around it.
siteSettings.aboutOrigin:
My route into product started in agriculture and operations. I studied Agricultural Administration, then became COO at MyFarmbase Africa, helping scale an EdTech and agribusiness platform to 9,000+ active users across West Africa and supporting the launch of 200+ profitable agribusinesses. Automating training workflows reduced administrative overhead by over 50%.

That experience still shapes how I work: understand the people, map the process, and find where the system breaks. Today, I apply that approach to commerce products at QShop and enterprise delivery at Yoke Solutions, from customer discovery and prioritisation through to execution.
siteSettings.aboutOperatingInstinct:
I enjoy sitting with users, understanding their problems, and turning what I learn into a direction the team can act on. I connect that discovery to business priorities, scoped plans, and prototypes that make decisions easier.

Delivery is part of that responsibility. I work with founders, engineers, designers, and client stakeholders to set priorities, manage scope, and keep work moving. Sometimes the right decision is a better activation flow; sometimes it is self-service tooling that removes recurring work; sometimes it is stopping an idea whose dependencies do not add up.
siteSettings.aboutCommunity: As Programme Lead for Morph by TNX Solve, I design programme and operational infrastructure for a teen product-development programme. I also facilitated an AI and no-code train-the-trainer workshop for Global Shapers Ota Hub, taking participants from problem definition to working prototypes. As a volunteer board member at Adlai Heroes Foundation, I advise on programme strategy, operations, and digital-product initiatives.
siteSettings.signoffText: Looking for a product manager who can connect customer discovery, operational detail, and delivery? Let’s talk.

qshop.tagline: Improving merchant activation, internal operations, and delivery across a commerce portfolio.

sections.label: Context
sections.body: I own product strategy for a commerce portfolio representing 59,700+ registered stores, $5.2M in annual GMV, and 18,000+ monthly orders. My work spans customer activation, merchant workflows, internal tooling, and team delivery.

sections.label: Activation
sections.body: I redesigned the activation flow through structured, hypothesis-led experimentation, reducing onboarding drop-off from 70% to 45%. I also decreased time-to-first-sale for new merchants by 15% and launched promotion and discovery features that boosted store-level order volume.

sections.label: Operational leverage
sections.body: I extended the admin surface so internal teams could self-serve five recurring request types. Addressing these requests at the source reduced the workload passed to support and engineering.

sections.label: How I lead
sections.body: I report directly to the founder and manage an associate PM. I set sprint delivery priorities to focus engineering effort and improved overall throughput by approximately 30%.

sections.label: Outcome
sections.body: The activation work reduced drop-off by 25 percentage points. The broader portfolio figures describe the scale of my product responsibility; they are not attributed to one experiment.

features.name: Time-to-first-sale
features.detail: Reduced the time new merchants took to reach their first sale.

features.name: Self-service tooling
features.detail: Enabled internal teams to handle recurring actions without support and engineering queues.

features.name: Delivery throughput
features.detail: Set sprint priorities and supervised an associate PM to improve engineering output.

qtrack.tagline: Knowing when to stop: what 500+ users taught me about a WhatsApp expense tracker.

sections.label: Problem
sections.body: I explored whether a WhatsApp expense tracker could make expense tracking easier to adopt.

sections.label: What I tested
sections.body: I validated the product with 500+ users, examining the behavioural and technical dependencies needed for continued investment.

sections.label: Decision
sections.body: The initiative depended on substantial behaviour change and unviable bank-API requirements. I made the strategic decision to discontinue it.

sections.label: What I learned
sections.body: Early adoption did not resolve the dependencies behind sustained use. The next product decision had to account for those constraints, rather than treat the user count as sufficient validation.

features.name: Early adoption
features.detail: Tested a WhatsApp expense-tracking product with real users.

features.name: Investment decision
features.detail: Stopped the initiative after identifying behavioural and bank-API dependencies.
